clue.text: Recorded snub

definitions.meaning: first meaning: written down, as a minute or an entry is
second meaning: a cutting remark that belittles someone

explanation.surface: Someone captures a rebuff on tape or in writing.
explanation.walkthrough: As a phrasal verb the answer means set down in writing; run together as a noun it is a humiliating remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one phrase: the verb for writing something down in a record, and the noun for a belittling rejoinder.

clue.text: Pushy type for the high jump

definitions.note: cryptic: a start that goes up
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a leap upwards from a standstill

explanation.surface: An ambitious person is in for severe punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'for the high jump' is British slang for being about to be punished; here it is read as a literal upward leap.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen who behaves presumptuously, and split it is a spring upward.

clue.text: The wastage is very large among doctors

indicators.note: being among a group places the first item inside the second

parts.note: standard abbreviation for doctors
OS is the clothing label for outsize

explanation.surface: Hospital waste is enormous where physicians work.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-size abbreviation for very large.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is scum or worthless refuse, the rubbish left over as waste.

clue.text: Term commonly used for a thrashing — why?

definitions.text: Term commonly used for a thrashing
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give someone this is to punish them
second meaning: the two-word question asking the reason

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a beating is called by a particular colloquial name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give him what for' is colloquial for a severe telling-off or beating.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for a punishing scolding, and literally a question demanding a reason.

clue.text: A house on mains supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, pliantly, so the preceding letters bend into a new shape

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: An estate agent notes that a property is connected to the mains utilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the utility noun, but read as 'supplely' it tells you to bend the letters of 'on mains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large and stately residence, a grand example of a dwelling.

clue.text: Fall to the Americans

parts.note: surface reading: a defeat or capture by US forces
setter's reading: Fall is the US word for a season, and the British name for it is wanted

explanation.surface: A city or army surrenders to American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Inverted: the Americans' word is in the clue, and the answer is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English the season between summer and winter is called the fall.

clue.text: Perhaps a pony is a matter of no consequence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pony is a small measure of ale, an example of a little drink

explanation.surface: A little horse is dismissed as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is old British slang for a small glass of beer, and also for £25, which itself is a trifling sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for trivial things, originally weak ale; a pony glass is a modest serving.

clue.text: A number making a noise in examination

indicators.note: one part sits inside the other that follows

parts.note: first half of an oral, a spoken test
a din is a loud noise
second half of the spoken test

explanation.surface: Something noisy happens during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: An oral is a spoken examination; the noise word sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers such as first and second express position in a sequence.

clue.text: A plan that goes into great detail

definitions.text: A plan that goes into great detail

parts.words: A plan that goes into great detail
parts.note: surface reading: a thorough scheme or strategy
setter's reading: a plan is a drawing of an area, and one showing great detail covers a small area at a big ratio

explanation.surface: A strategy that is worked out very thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plan' suggests a scheme, but it means a chart; great detail comes from a big representative fraction such as 1:1250.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartographic sheet drawn at a big ratio shows streets and buildings in fine detail over a small area.

clue.text: Capital invested in Czechoslovakia

indicators.note: money invested in a firm sits inside it, so the target lies within the following word

parts.note: letters five to eight of the country's name

explanation.surface: Money was put into the old Central European state's economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money invested; it is the definition, a capital city of another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the seat of government and chief city of Norway, hence a national capital.

clue.text: Way-out of the theatre

parts.note: surface reading: an exit leading out of a playhouse
setter's reading: way-out means wildly unconventional, and the clue asks for the experimental wing of drama

explanation.surface: A sign pointing to the exit of a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen is the giveaway: way-out is slang for weird or radical, describing experimental stagecraft rather than a door.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde art and drama is experimental and radical, exactly what slang calls way-out, applied here to stage work.

clue.text: High range of service provided

parts.note: a church service, the Eucharist
provided that, on condition

explanation.surface: A wide range of service is on offer from a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High range of service' reads like a quality claim; 'high range' is a mountain group.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming an upland block, so a lofty range.

clue.text: Taking a stroll after midnight is taking a risk

indicators.note: coming after something means placed behind it, so the stroll goes second

parts.note: the middle of night is its central letter, the third of five
walking at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Walking about in the small hours could be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' looks like a time, but it is the middle of 'night'; 'after' places the stroll after that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling means staking money or safety on an uncertain outcome, i.e. hazarding something.

clue.text: Cease to insist on the latest news

parts.note: halt, come to an end
to press is to urge or insist

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop demanding to hear what has just happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop press is the late column a newspaper added after printing began.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop-press items are last-minute reports inserted into a newspaper after its main printing run started.

clue.text: Joke will end with a periodical row

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: what a joke ends with

parts.note: Punch was a famous British humour magazine
a line, a row of things

explanation.surface: A comic tale finishes with a quarrel at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodical' looks like an adjective, recurring; it is a noun, a magazine. 'Row' is a line, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The punchline is the final sentence that delivers a joke's payoff.

clue.text: A sweet sort of baby

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wobbly gelatine dessert

definitions.note: the answer is the word that precedes baby in that sweet's name
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ... baby is a baby-shaped gummy sweet

explanation.surface: A cute infant is described as lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sweet sort of baby' reads as praise for a child; jelly babies are British gummy sweets shaped like infants.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly is a set gelatine pudding, and it names one type of baby-shaped confectionery.

clue.text: Stretch over the end of the desk and chastise

parts.note: an extent or stretch of distance or time

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A child is bent over the edge of a desk and punished.
explanation.definitionFit: To spank is to slap the buttocks as punishment, a physical way to discipline.

clue.text: An empty new settlement

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A recently built village with no residents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' suggests a village; it means the settling of a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlement of an account is the act of paying what is owed.

clue.text: Just buying and selling

parts.note: just means fair, equitable
commerce, exchange of goods

explanation.surface: A merchant insists their commerce is entirely honest and above board.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the ethical-sourcing movement; split, it gives the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair trade is commerce that pays producers equitably, so equitable commerce is precisely what it names.

clue.text: Gather that the boxer is slightly in the lead?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to herd or collect together

definitions.text: the boxer is slightly in the lead
definitions.note: cryptic: a fighter one round ahead
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split: a fighter ahead by one bout segment

explanation.surface: Apparently the fighter has a narrow advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather that' reads as 'I understand'; 'Gather' alone is the definition, the rest a jokey scoring description.
explanation.definitionFit: To round up cattle or suspects is to collect them together in one place.

clue.text: Saving Grace

parts.note: surface reading: a redeeming quality
setter's reading: the surname of the Victorian lighthouse keeper's daughter famous for a sea rescue

explanation.surface: The one redeeming feature of something otherwise poor.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling rowed out in 1838 to rescue shipwreck survivors off Northumberland; the answer is also a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace Darling became a British national heroine for saving survivors of the wrecked steamer Forfarshire.

clue.text: Near the brink and very nervous

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at the very rim of something

explanation.surface: Someone close to a precipice is understandably anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally at the rim of a drop, and figuratively tense or jittery.

clue.text: Near fortune acquired through luck

parts.note: close by, nearby
luck, fate

explanation.surface: Someone nearly came into a fortune purely through good luck.
explanation.definitionFit: By chance means accidentally, happening without design, owing to fortune alone.

clue.text: Recovery vessel — put out in it

indicators.note: something put out of order is disarranged, so the word is reworked

parts.note: the word as written, then rearranged
a vase or container

explanation.surface: A salvage ship sets out to raise a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recovery vessel' looks like one salvage boat; the definition is only 'Recovery', in the economic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an improvement in fortunes, as when markets climb back after a slump.

clue.text: Uplifted, achieved very good times

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: met a target, achieved it
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: Elated after achieving excellent results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' are musical speeds here, the plural of tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the Italian plural of tempo, the speeds at which pieces of music are played.

clue.text: Where to yawn, when it's late

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: politely, a yawn goes behind a raised palm

explanation.surface: Good manners advise covering a yawn as the night grows late.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the answer is the polite spot to yawn; whole, it means running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand describes someone overdue or in arrears with work or payments, i.e. tardy.

clue.text: Post of bodyguard

definitions.meaning: second meaning: chain armour that protects a knight's torso

explanation.surface: A job as someone's personal protector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post of bodyguard' reads as a job vacancy; here 'bodyguard' is literal, a guard for the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is letters sent by the postal service, and also flexible metal-ring armour worn to protect a fighter.

clue.text: Wrested apart and scattered

indicators.note: pulled apart, the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the word as written

explanation.surface: Things were torn away and flung about.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to spread things untidily over a surface, so strewn items are dispersed.

clue.text: Broken spy ring likely to bounce back

indicators.note: a broken ring is smashed up, so its letters are put together differently

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: An espionage network smashed by police may reform afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy is elastic and resilient, recovering its shape when pressed.
